subject: Re: DPA annex - learning toggle + evidence flow for Halo Analytics
messages:
From: Alicia Byrne <alicia@haloanalytics.com>

Subject: DPA annex - proposed 'learning' carveout and evidence request

Hi Olga / Redwood team,

Attaching a first pass at a short annex to our DPA. We need an explicit commitment that Halo Analytics data will not be used to improve or retrain models (no-learning) except where anonymized, aggregated telemetry is used for platform stability (not model weights). We also want a practical evidence flow: periodic attestations and an emergency export for audit.

Key asks:
- Clear definition of what constitutes 'training' vs. operational telemetry
- A technical outline for how prompt/response pairs are excluded from model improvement
- Timeframe for producing evidence (we'd like quarterly attestations and a one-week turnaround for ad-hoc evidence requests)

We attached our proposed language (Halo_DPA_Annex_v1.pdf) and a redline doc. Can you confirm what evidence you can produce and whether Redwood can accept the no-learning carveout for our account?

Thanks,
Alicia Byrne
Head of Security & Compliance
Halo Analytics

Attachments: Halo_DPA_Annex_v1.pdf, Halo_HighLevel_Redlines.docx
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Byrne <alicia@haloanalytics.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-10T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA annex - proposed 'learning' carveout and evidence request

Hi Alicia — thanks for the draft and the clear asks. High-level reply below; technical follow-up from Dev and a proposed evidence cadence attached (redwood-evidence-guidelines.pdf).

Short answers:
- We can agree to a contractual no-learning commitment scoped to customer-provided production traffic (prompts and responses) being excluded from model improvement, with a narrow exception for aggregated telemetry for platform health (latency/error metrics only).
- We need to align on definitions — we propose:
  • "Model improvement/training": any process that updates model weights or fine-tunes model parameters using customer data.
  • "Operational telemetry": aggregated metrics (e.g., mean latency, error rates) where individual prompt/response pairs are not reconstructible.
- Evidence: Redwood can provide quarterly attestations and a time-boxed ad-hoc evidence package (logs + attestation) within 7 business days for standard requests. For forensic exports that include non-anonymized content we need a data access agreement and scoped SFTP/secure transfer.

Open items for your team to confirm:
1) Are system logs that include request IDs acceptable, or do you need full prompt/response exports for ad-hoc audits?
2) Do you require cryptographic hashing of prompt identifiers to demonstrate exclusion?
3) Is the quarterly cadence sufficient, or do you want monthly attestations for the first 3 months after go-live?

I've looped in Dev (technical) and Laura (legal/program owner) to help pin details. Next steps: if you agree with the scope above we'll circulate redline language that formalizes the no-learning clause and the evidence SLA.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Trust & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Hi Alicia — quick technical note on how we can operationalize the exclusion so it's auditable without exposing customer data:

1) Request tagging: we can accept a per-customer header (X-Redwood-NoTrain: true) on API calls. Requests with that header are written to a segregated append-only bucket and are never routed to model-improvement pipelines.

2) Deterministic hashing: for auditability we compute a SHA-256 hash (salted) of prompts and responses server-side and store only the hash and a timestamp. Hashes prove the presence/absence of items without revealing content. If Halo needs full content for an audit, we can run an export under a joint-agreed data access process.

3) Telemetry: aggregated metrics (p90 latency, error counts) will be available in the Console; we can produce CSV extracts for attestations.

Implementation note: adding the header is the simplest path. If you cannot modify calls, we can provision a dedicated ingest endpoint or a routing policy for traffic from your account to mark it as excluded.

Happy to hop on a short call with your SRE to align on the header/endpoint option.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Olga and Dev — this is helpful and close to what we need. A few notes on Halo's side after an internal review:

- Request IDs + salted hashes are acceptable for quarterly attestation. For ad-hoc audits, we will request full prompt/response exports in a narrow set of circumstances (incidence reviews or regulatory requests). We accept the need for a scoped data access agreement for those exports.
- For the header approach: our gateway can inject X-Redwood-NoTrain: true for production traffic within two weeks of PO. We'd like a short transition period during which both header and account-level routing will be honored.
- We have two redlines attached (Halo_HighLevel_Redlines.docx). Our legal asks for a 7-business-day SLAT for ad-hoc evidence deliveries and quarterly attestations for the first 6 months, then move to quarterly afterwards.

Can you confirm acceptance of the 6-month elevated cadence and the transition approach? If yes, we'll circulate the PO and the annex for signature.

Alicia Byrne
Head of Security & Compliance
Halo Analytics
